correctness.rationale: Reconstructed Fourier normalization, radial transform, homogeneous-distribution coefficient 2^(d+alpha)π^(d/2)Γ((d+alpha)/2)/Γ(-alpha/2), and derivative at alpha=2 C_d=2^(d+1)π^(d/2)Γ((d+2)/2)>0. With a smooth cutoff at the origin, the p-derivative of e^(-|x|^p) at p2 has a negative r^(-d-2) tail and error O(r^(-d-4)log r); the second exponent derivative is bounded uniformly for q∈[2,2+eps0], r>=2 by O(r^(-d-2)(1+log²r)), yielding uniform Taylor control. At r_±²/4=L+(d+2)/2 log L+log(2/Γ((d+2)/2))±δ the Gaussian-to-negative-tail ratio tends to e^(∓δ). It is monotone decreasing past fixed large r, while compact r remains positive by convergence to the strictly positive Gaussian. This excludes earlier zeros and brackets the first. Fresh independent high-precision differentiation verified C_d for d=1..6, not a proof of the uniform cutoff bound. The standard cutoff lemma is the main analytic dependency and the proof states its required range.
